Hi Ava — thanks for the heads-up and the summary. Wed 11/4 10:30 PT works for our team; booking now.

Quick notes before the sync (we attached a short snapshot):
- High-level numbers (run on our dedicated staging pool, M40-equivalent): p50 ~ 60ms, p95 ~ 210ms, p99 ~ 480ms for 512-token prompts at 8-token/sec generation. Throughput observed ~ 180 tokens/sec per GPU under continuous batching policy.
- Variability is concentrated on tail due to KV cache misses in multi-session runs; likely tuning target #1.
- Proposed immediate tuning steps to discuss: reduce max batch size to limit head-of-line blocking; enable per-customer KV cache pinning for NovaHealth; try int8 quant profile on a canary model variant.

Attaching: perf_snapshot_q3.csv (sample run), MAP_v3_NovaHealth.pdf (updated MAP with evaluation criteria). Also shared a Drive folder with raw logs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B-map-notes-NovaHealth

Looking forward to the sync — will bring Marissa and Vivek to walk through numbers and owners.

Best,
Soojin Lee

Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 11:21:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MAP checkpoint: performance evaluation & tuning actions for NovaHealth

Thanks for the sync earlier — quick technical follow-ups from our side (pulled from the meeting recording and logs):

- Confirmed numbers (512-token prompts, multi-session load): p50 58ms, p95 205ms, p99 475ms. Peak throughput observed with continuous batching: ~1.6k tokens/sec for the pool (8 GPUs), ~200 tokens/sec/GPU.
- Root cause hypothesis: KV cache churn when sessions spike + aggressive batching leads to occasional kernel scheduling stalls.
- Immediate canary actions (propose owners & ETA):
  * Reduce default max_batch_size from 64 -> 32 for NovaHealth route — Owner: Marissa; ETA: 48 hours.
  * Enable per-route KV cache pinning (persist prefetched KV for warmed sessions) — Owner: Vivek; ETA: 72 hours.
  * Run int8 quantized canary on model v2-quant (quality check required) — Owner: Karthik; ETA: 5 business days.
  * Add prefix caching for common prompts used in evaluation set — Owner: NovaHealth infra (Ava/Theo); Redwood to assist with suggested prompt fingerprinting.

Risks & rollback: if int8 canary shows >1% delta on Rouge/QA metrics, we will auto-roll back to baseline model and keep batching/caching changes.

I've uploaded raw CSV and a short checklist to the shared folder.

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference

Subject: MAP checkpoint summary & action owners — NovaHealth (closed-loop)

Hi team —

Thanks for a productive checkpoint. Summary and explicit action items below (so we have closed-loop ownership and dates).

Meeting summary (short): p95/p99 tail driven by KV cache churn under multi-session spikes; batching configuration amplifies head-of-line waits. We agreed on a canary-first approach to minimize risk to quality while addressing latency tails.

Action items (owner — ETA)
- Marissa: deploy reduced max_batch_size (64->32) to NovaHealth route in staging and run 24h soak — ETA: 2026-11-07 EOD.
- Vivek: enable per-route KV cache pinning + monitor cache hit ratio; provide alert if p95 increases >10% — ETA: 2026-11-08 EOD.
- Karthik: run int8 quant canary on v2-quant, collect quality metrics vs baseline (automated eval set from MAP) — ETA: 2026-11-11 COB.
- NovaHealth (Ava/Theo): share top-15 prompts and traffic fingerprints for prefix caching suggestion — ETA: 2026-11-06 EOD.
- Soojin: update MAP_v3_NovaHealth.pdf with these owners & closure criteria; share updated MAP and confirm pilot start date once canaries are green — ETA: 2026-11-09.

Attachments: perf_snapshot_q3.csv, MAP_v3_NovaHealth.pdf. Drive notes + raw logs are in the linked folder.

Next checkpoint: 2026-11-10 10:00 PT (30m) — resume with canary metrics + go/no-go recommendation.

If anything needs to shift, flag in the HubSpot deal (NH-2026-87) and I'll escalate.
